claims.rule: Review a custom Fail overload against distinct oracles for failure index, custom label and verbose/replay behavior. Preserve the existing verboseFailures policy while ensuring the supplied message is actually reported; reject tests that accidentally assert the old default label.
claims.applicability: PR 244 supplies an explicit mode-preservation review and a post-merge counterexample. PR 297 merge commit 49ba3cf46705a5068541537991ce1c2167760a2b on 2023-11-26 corrects both the reporting closure and custom-label trace assertion. The ordinary/verbose/replay matrix is an inference from Parsed.Extra.trace and BufferedParserInput, not a claim that the historical fix exercised every row. Integration failures and first released version remain distinct from the source correction.
claims.counterexample: A nonverbose failure with no label is not itself a bug. Replaying a consumed iterator is explicitly unsupported in the sampled implementation, so demanding trace() success for it would be a false positive.

claims.rule: For a wrapper parser that hides or negates its child (opaque, unary_!, or a new combinator with that intent), snapshot the append-only terminal aggregate before running the child and, under verboseFailures, restore it before reporting the wrapper's own label. Test with a deterministic trace() that asserts the aggregate, message and terminals views separately.
claims.applicability: Inference from author source comments, commit rationale and regression tests of PRs 276/278 (2023, Fastparse 3.0 line; the field was renamed terminalParserMsgs to terminalMsgs between them). There was no reviewer discussion on PR 278. Index, success and cut must stay outside the verbose guard.
claims.counterexample: A transparent wrapper (for example a named rule or a logging wrapper) should keep child terminals; resetting them would hide useful expectations. Narrowed downstream terminal snapshots (PR 278 narrowed four ScalaParse expectations) are intended when the wrapper is meant to be opaque.
